component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the engagement against the RFP Schedule of Events, with all meetings and events held between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central. The team facilitates a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to agree a protocol for ongoing communications and coordination, then holds quarterly project status meetings reviewing progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next, and produces written minutes for the kick-off and for every quarterly status meeting. Monthly e-mail and phone contact with MoDOT contacts keeps progress visible between meetings, and quarterly updates on work accomplished are submitted on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December so they feed the SPR Quarterly Report MoDOT submits to FHWA. The project manager coordinates all activities with the Construction and Materials Division, keeps advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division as work progresses, and consults MHTC's representative on any concern about administration of the services. An interim presentation is scheduled near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and direction. The team also plans and tracks the full milestone chain: the 4/25/2025 demonstration of how the AI/ML creates draft LLDs, the 7/25/2025 training and manual, the 11/3/2025 draft final report, summary report and user manual, the 1/1/2026 final documents and the 2/2/2026 final invoice and contract end, with draft documents issued roughly two months before the final report and final documents roughly one month before contract end.

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML right of way practice
component_records.description: The team conducts a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right of way purposes, covering published research, DOT reports and documented pilots, and records the methods, data sources and outcomes found. Findings are written up as a standalone review chapter that feeds the Synthesis Report and the final report, and are presented at the first quarterly status meeting so MoDOT can steer the proof-of-concept scope. The review also identifies which drafting rules and quality checks other states apply, which informs the MHTC parameter set used in the tool.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of the kick-off meeting the team submits a Data Management Plan to MoDOT that describes the anticipated formats of the project data and related files, naming the file types for source deeds, right of way plans, survey data, training data and generated drafts. The plan commits to platform-independent and non-proprietary formats for all data and deliverables so MoDOT can reuse them after the contract, and sets out retention, access and handover arrangements consistent with MHTC ownership of all materials produced at its direction. The plan is maintained through the project and updated at each quarterly status meeting.

component_records.title: AI/ML legal land description drafting tool: selection, approval and build
component_records.description: The team names the program it will use to develop legal land descriptions before proof-of-concept work begins and submits it to MoDOT Information Systems for approval, holding Task 3c until that approval is recorded. The tool is built or configured to apply the MHTC parameters and the drafting rules of MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, generating a first draft that MoDOT Right of Way staff can review and edit in the tool. Drafting logic enforces the metes and bounds method for partial acquisitions, reproduces the last deed of record verbatim where a property is acquired in its entirety, and recites the specific rights being acquired, conveyed or leased where those rights are less than fee simple, described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls. A professional land surveyor sits in the review loop and checks each generated description against the right of way plans and the gathered survey information before any deed is presented to the grantor. The application is developed on a currently supported .NET 6.0 or above release using C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team approves larger use; web components use MVC, Razor Pages or Web API; library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually; and no third-party tool that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT is used without prior BRPT and IS management approval. The application is web-based and runs in a modern browser with no client-side software such as Java Applets or Silverlight, is tested against the latest IS approved browsers, and meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508. It stores no PII in any database table unless a specific business need is approved by the IS Cyber Security Team, and any on-premise database runs on Oracle 19C. No vendor logos or branding appear where a licensed option exists to remove them, and no third-party text, images, code or graphics are used without permission or a free-copy licence.

component_records.title: Proof of concept and MoDOT feedback cycles
component_records.description: The team demonstrates how its technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, using MoDOT-supplied property records and right of way plans, and MoDOT reviews the drafts and returns improvement feedback. On 4/25/2025 the team presents how the AI/ML creates draft LLDs and incorporates that feedback into the tool. Each cycle records the drafting errors found, the parameter or prompt changes made and the resulting accuracy, so the usefulness of AI/ML for a first draft is evidenced rather than asserted. The proof-of-concept results form the core findings of the final report.

component_records.title: Finalisation, user manual and Right of Way staff training
component_records.description: After adjustments are made to the tool, the team finalises the system and produces a user manual for staff reference, then delivers training to Right of Way staff by 7/25/2025 covering how to generate, review and edit a first draft and how to check it against right of way plans. Training is delivered in sessions at MoDOT premises with a recorded walkthrough for staff who cannot attend, and the manual is issued in both editable and PDF form. The manual and training materials are updated after MoDOT review and reissued with the 11/3/2025 draft deliverables and the 1/1/2026 final deliverables.

component_records.title: Synthesis Report, final report, research summary and presentation
component_records.description: The team prepares a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary together with the accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study, delivered as final products except for revisions arising from MoDOT's review. The final report details every task completed and all findings generated during the project, including the literature review, proof-of-concept results and the assessed usefulness of AI/ML for first-draft LLDs. A 1-2 page research summary states the project objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff summarises the significant details of the project. Drafts are issued on 11/3/2025 and finals on 1/1/2026, with the interim presentation near mid-point covering progress and direction.

component_records.title: Contract, compliance and commercial obligations
component_records.description: A contract and compliance workstream carries the non-technical obligations of the bid. It prepares the fee proposal on the PRICE PAGE and the cost estimate on Section (4) of the proposal, broken down into Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total, with Miscellaneous costs itemised on an additional sheet, covering all services in the Scope of Work and held within the $175,000 ceiling; the Offeror commits to provide the services at the fees quoted. The workstream confirms the Offeror is a qualified research organisation, submits the proposal on the basis that it is open to public inspection without reservation, and accepts that the award is a post-award negotiated contract on the RFP provisions, with MHTC free to cancel the award if terms cannot be agreed. It maintains the General Liability cover of $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Automobile Liability cover at the same limits, and a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy, and can furnish certificates of insurance before signing. It runs the employment-eligibility controls: certification that assigned employees are authorised to work in the United States, no knowing employment of unauthorised aliens, E-Verify enrolment evidenced by the MOU, a sworn affidavit of non-employment of unauthorised aliens, and affirmative proof of lawful presence for each sole proprietor or general partner. It writes the required flow-down provisions into every subcontract, takes the enforcement action the Commission directs including sanctions for noncompliance, and remains fully liable to MHTC for the quality and performance of subcontractors and suppliers. It secures MHTC consent before releasing any material or report to the public, keeps MHTC information confidential and notifies MHTC immediately of any request for confidential information, and confirms MHTC ownership of all documents, reports and materials produced at its direction. It keeps working papers available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor during the Agreement and for three years from final payment, supports MHTC's right to audit all records and to reproduce and use products royalty-free, complies with Executive Order 07-13 and with FFATA reporting and 2 C.F.R. Part 170 award terms, and routes any change in the Agreement through a formal amendment signed by both authorised representatives. The workstream also records the MBE and WBE participation targets of 10% and 5% in the subcontracting plan and reports progress against them.

items.text: EPG Section 236.4.6.2 drafting rules are not in the RFP. The RFP requires every generated description to meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 but does not reproduce it, and the proposed solution assumes the section contains only the metes and bounds, deed-of-record and rights-recital rules quoted in the RFP. If the section carries further rules on calls, monuments, area statements or format, the drafting logic and the proof-of-concept results would need rework after the tool is built. The drafting rule set is the core of the tool, so a wrong rule set means rebuilding the generation logic and re-running the demonstration; the RFP does not supply the section, so the likelihood turns on a document the bidder has not seen.
items.reason: Cited sources show EPG 236.4.6.2 is referenced and only the quoted rules are in the RFP; the risk judgment needs no support.

items.text: Program approval gate can stall the proof of concept. The RFP requires MoDOT Information Systems to approve the named program before Task 3c may proceed, but sets no approval turnaround and no consequence if approval is delayed or refused. The proposed solution assumes approval within four weeks of the kick-off meeting. A longer review, or a refusal of the chosen program, would push the 4/25/2025 demonstration and every later milestone. The 4/25/2025 demonstration is a fixed contractual date and the whole milestone chain sits behind the approval gate, so a slip here misses a contractual date; the RFP gives no turnaround, so the likelihood turns on MoDOT's internal review.
items.reason: Approval requirement before Task 3c and the 4/25/2025 demonstration are stated; no turnaround is given. Four-week assumption is the bidder's position.

items.text: Budget cap below the likely build cost. The RFP caps the services at $175,000 for a 15-month engagement that includes a literature review, an AI/ML tool build, a proof of concept on multiple properties, a user manual, staff training and four reports. The proposed solution treats the figure as a firm all-inclusive ceiling and prices the proof of concept on ten properties and training for fifteen staff. If the tool build or the property volume runs larger than assumed, the bidder absorbs the overrun, and the RFP does not say whether the cap may be revised. A build of this scope against a fixed ceiling can overrun by more than a quarter if the property count or the drafting rules grow, and the RFP leaves the ceiling's firmness open, so the likelihood turns on facts the RFP does not settle.
items.reason: $175,000 cap and 15 months are stated; the 'four reports' and 'multiple properties' scope details are not in the cited sources.

items.text: Exhibit A and Exhibit B are referenced but not supplied. The RFP requires a sworn affidavit of non-employment of unauthorized aliens attached as Exhibit A and a sworn affidavit of lawful presence attached as Exhibit B, but neither exhibit is in the document. The bid team cannot confirm the wording, the signatories or the notarisation requirements, and a defective affidavit is a responsiveness defect that can disqualify the proposal. The exhibits are missing from the RFP as issued, so the bidder will not have the correct forms unless it asks; the consequence is a submission defect rather than a delivery failure, which keeps severity at medium.
items.reason: Exhibits A and B are referenced, but the cited sources do not show they are missing from the document; the notarisation point is also unsupported.

items.text: Contract end date conflicts with the 15-month term. The RFP says the contract runs 15 months from a November 1, 2024 start, which would end around 1/31/2026, but also fixes the contract end and final invoice at 2/2/2026. The proposed solution prices and schedules to the 2/2/2026 date. If MoDOT treats the 15-month count as controlling, the last days of reporting and invoicing fall outside the term and the final invoice may be rejected or the work compressed. The two dates differ by only a few days, so the cost impact is small, but the final invoice is the payment event and the RFP does not say which date governs. The solution resolves the conflict by assumption rather than by asking.
items.reason: 15-month term, 2/2/2026 end date and November 1, 2024 start estimate are all in the sources; the date conflict is a fair reading.

items.text: Draft and final deliverable dates conflict with the lead-time rules. The RFP fixes the draft final report, summary report and user manual at 11/3/2025 and the final documents at 1/1/2026, but also requires drafts about two months before the final report and finals about one month before contract end. Read literally, the two-month rule would pull the drafts to early November 2025 only if the final report is 1/1/2026, and the one-month rule would pull finals to early January 2026. The bid team cannot tell which date triggers acceptance and payment, and a wrong reading risks a rejected deliverable or a missed billing window. The dates are close enough that the cost is a slip rather than a failure, but acceptance and billing depend on the date MoDOT applies and the RFP does not settle it. The solution assumes the listed dates control.
items.reason: Dates of 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 and the two-month and one-month lead-time rules are all stated in the sources.

items.text: MHTC parameters are undefined and drive the training data. The RFP requires the first draft to be generated using the MHTC parameters but never defines them, and the proposed solution assumes they are the EPG drafting conventions plus MoDOT right of way plan formats. If the parameters include district-specific conventions, deed language preferences or a house style, the tool would need retraining and the proof-of-concept results would not transfer to production use. Parameter definition changes the design and the training effort but not the overall feasibility of the study, and the RFP leaves it open, so the likelihood depends on facts the RFP does not give.
items.reason: RFP uses MHTC parameters without defining them in cited sources; other content is proposed-solution assumption and risk judgment.

items.text: Python approval gate before the proof of concept. The RFP confines Python to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team approves larger use, and the proposed solution relies on Python for the AI/ML work. If the drafting engine needs substantial Python, the team must wait for BRPT and IS management approval, which the RFP does not time, and the build schedule and the 4/25/2025 demonstration are at risk. The solution already commits to confining Python, so the exposure is a design constraint and a possible approval delay rather than a certain failure; the RFP does not define what counts as large-scale use or how long approval takes.
items.reason: Python restriction, BRPT approval, and 4/25/2025 date are in sources; the rest is judgment about the bidder's solution.

items.text: Oracle 19C and SQL Server requirements conflict. The RFP requires on-premise databases to run on Oracle 19C in one place and permits Microsoft SQL Server 2016 or higher with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval in another. The proposed solution treats Oracle 19C as the primary option. If MoDOT's environment is SQL Server based, the team would build against the wrong platform and rework the data layer, and Oracle licensing on an on-premise deployment is a cost the $175,000 ceiling may not carry. The database choice affects build effort and licensing cost but not the feasibility of the study, and the RFP leaves the choice open, so the likelihood depends on MoDOT's actual environment.
items.reason: Oracle/SQL Server rules supported; the $175,000 ceiling is not in the cited sources.

items.text: Two pages of the RFP could not be read. Pages 19 and 20 of the RFP carry almost no extractable text and are dominated by images, so any requirement, form or table on those pages is invisible to the bid team. If those pages hold a submission form, a pricing table or a deliverable specification, the proposal could omit required content or misprice a task. The pages sit in the section covering the kick-off, Data Management Plan and quarterly meetings, so they may hold only narrative, but the bidder cannot confirm that; an omitted form is a responsiveness defect.
items.reason: Cited sources say nothing about pages 19-20 being unreadable; they only state kick-off, DMP and quarterly meetings.

items.text: Proof-of-concept property volume and data supply are undefined. The RFP requires a demonstration on a variety of properties but does not say how many, of what type, or who supplies the records and right of way plans. The proposed solution prices ten properties of mixed type supplied by MoDOT. If MoDOT supplies fewer properties, supplies them late, or expects the bidder to source them, the demonstration effort and the 4/25/2025 date are at risk. The demonstration is a fixed milestone and the effort scales with property count, but the RFP leaves the count and the data supply open, so the likelihood depends on MoDOT's answer.
items.reason: Variety of properties, 4/25/2025 demonstration and absence of count or data supply details are consistent with sources.

items.text: Work Plan page limit is stated as both a cap and a preference. The RFP caps the Work Plan at ten pages in one place and excludes forms and resumes from the limit in another, and the requirement is phrased with should. The proposed solution treats the ten-page limit as mandatory. If the limit is enforced strictly, a plan that carries the full milestone chain and technical approach may be cut for space; if it is only a preference, the bidder may have over-compressed the plan and lost evaluation points. The consequence is a re-cut of a proposal section, which normal delivery absorbs, and the RFP leaves the limit's status open, so the likelihood depends on how MoDOT reads its own text.
items.reason: Cap and exclusions supported; the claim that the requirement is phrased with 'should' is accurate, but a conflict between cap and preference is overstated.
